skill.name: Web Font Rendering Strategy Selection
skill.description: Select between FOUT (Flash of Unstyled Text) and FOIT (Flash of Invisible Text) rendering strategies when web fonts are loading, based on user experience priorities and content visibility requirements.
skill.skill_body:
When a web font is downloading, the browser must decide how to render text before the font arrives. Evaluate whether users should see unstyled text immediately (FOUT) or invisible text until the font is ready (FOIT). Choose the strategy that best balances content visibility, layout stability, and user experience for your use case.

## Objective

Choose appropriate web font rendering fallback strategy to minimize layout shift and optimize user experience during font loading
## Applicable Signals

- Web font download in progress
- Fallback font available and ready to render
- User interaction or page load phase where text rendering strategy matters

## Contraindications

- Web fonts are already cached or pre-loaded
- System fonts only are being used
- Font loading is not a performance concern
- No fallback font is available

## Intervention Moves

- If users need immediate access to content: recommend FOUT (fallback font swaps with web font)
- If layout stability is paramount: recommend FOIT (text invisible until web font ready)

## Workflow Steps

- {'step': 1, 'action': 'Assess content visibility priority', 'detail': 'Determine whether immediate text visibility (FOUT) or text invisibility until styled (FOIT) better serves your users'}
- {'step': 2, 'action': 'Evaluate layout shift tolerance', 'detail': 'Consider how much layout shift is acceptable when the web font swaps in and potentially changes text dimensions'}
- {'step': 3, 'action': 'Select rendering strategy', 'detail': 'Choose FOUT if content readability is critical; choose FOIT if layout stability is critical'}
- {'step': 4, 'action': 'Apply and document strategy', 'detail': 'Implement the selected strategy in font-loading CSS or JavaScript and document the choice for future maintenance'}

## Constraints

- Strategy must be selected before web font download completes
- Fallback font must be available for either strategy to work
- Choice affects both visual stability and perceived performance

## Cautions

- FOUT may cause visible text reflow when web font arrives
- FOIT may delay content visibility and harm perceived performance
- Strategy choice directly impacts Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) metrics

## Output Contract

- Selected rendering strategy (FOUT or FOIT) is applied and documented; layout shift impact during font swap is minimized and measurable
